body.x: The Smart Drone Technology Center of Kyungpook National University supported two companies - DROGEN and Rainbow Laboratory(RGBLAB), which are promising drone companies at ‘CES 2017’, held in Las Vegas from January 5th (Thursday) to 8th (Sunday).

The Smart Drone Technology Center of Kyungpook National University is an institute established to develop technologies needed for drone technology innovation and to spread them to the industrial world. It develops drone main boards, constructs infrastructure, creates drone ecosystem, and carries out unmanned airdrome test business.

From 2015 to 2019, this institute is carrying out a national project that worth 29 billion won. At CES 2017, it supported the participation of ‘DROGEN’, which develops racing drone, and ‘Rainbow Laboratory’, which develops main boards.
The director of this center, Lee Duk-Man, said “We will continue to make efforts to develop domestic drone technologies, including the support for related companies.”

On the other hand, Daegu Techno Park, the Smart Venture Business School of Kyungpook National Unviersity, and the Smart Drone Technology Center of Kyungpook National University opened CES Daegu Joint Pavilion and supported the exhibition management and business buyer consultation of 22 companies in Korea.

CES, the world’s largest IT Consumer Electronics Show, is an exhibition where the trends of the global electronic industry can be seen at a glimpse, and it is held in January every year by the American Consumer Technology Association (CTA).

Global News Network Aving News, which has reported the most recent issues of CES, MWC and IFA, the world’s top three technology exhibitions over the past decade, has also sent a special report team to CES this year, reporting on major issues of the market and introducing Korean companies to the world.
